steps.name: Nonce Audit
steps.detail: 138/138 epochs: single client seed each, nonces in capture order, unique, and exactly the DECLARED window [0, 49] (NONCE_BASE 0 and EXPECTED_EPOCH_SIZE 50 are code constants in src/pins.ts — not the minimum observed, and not the seed records' own nonceStart/nonceEnd, which are checked AGAINST the declaration: 0 disagreements). Gaps: 0 found, 0 capture-retry gap(s) declared. The window is what the capture requested under each seed, not an operator-side counter: this establishes that the bet rows are complete against it, not that no other nonce was ever served (selective orphaning — see MANIFEST.md#dataset-and-capture). No gaps in any epoch.

profileChecks.note: the client-seed half: per epoch exactly one client seed (Set size 1, otherwise HARD FAIL) — tests/steps/commitment.ts. The server-seed-hash half is Step 3

the window is DECLARED: every epoch's nonces must be exactly NONCE_BASE … NONCE_BASE+EXPECTED_EPOCH_SIZE−1 (src/pins.ts, 0 … 49) — a code constant, not the minimum observed and not the seed record's nonceStart, which is now checked AGAINST the declaration (a record/declaration disagreement hard-fails). steps.name: Mine-Layout Recomputation
steps.detail: 6900/6900 bets recomputed against the pinned population (src/pins.ts EXPECTED_BETS, a code constant — not bets.length, which would make this figure true of any capture); revealMines(serverSeed, clientSeed, nonce, mineCount) == mineTiles (draw order); 0 mismatches; 0 skipped (unrevealed seeds). Draw bias bound (declared design: rejection sampling, src/rng.ts maxFairFor): maxFair per range [range:maxFair] 25:4294967275 24:4294967280 23:4294967284 22:4294967292 21:4294967292 20:4294967280 19:4294967290 18:4294967292 17:4294967295 16:4294967296 15:4294967295 14:4294967292 13:4294967287 12:4294967292 11:4294967292 10:4294967290 9:4294967292 8:4294967296 7:4294967292 6:4294967292 5:4294967295 4:4294967296 3:4294967295 2:4294967296 1:4294967296; 25/25 ranges have maxFair a whole multiple of the range, so the per-value bias conditional on acceptance is exactly 0 (worst over all ranges 0; bound 2^-32 = 2.328e-10); per-draw rejection probability (2^32 − maxFair)/2^32 is at most 4.889e-9 (range 25). Rejection census over this population: 0 of 172500 draws (6900 rounds × 25) took the branch, against 2.024e-4 expected — the capture does not exercise it, so the branch is shown on a vector instead: nonce 760455, cursor 12, range 13 rejects its first chunk and draws 6 (expected 6; deleting the branch gives 1) OK. This bounds the AUDITOR'S draw; that the operator's server takes the same branch is ASSUMED (MANIFEST DL-3). Player-verifier parity (MINES-24): the ProvablyFair.org site verifier, vendored in verifier-parity/, games/mines/derive.js sha256 fa4dbd19b80e7ce7… = pin; lib/hmac-sha256.js sha256 2095571fecd77f53… = pin; its deriveMines was run on 6900/6900 captured rounds and matches src/rng.ts revealMines in draw order on 6900 (0 mismatches), and the served mineTiles on 6900; its displayCents equals src/config.ts minesMultiplierDisplayCents at 300/300 legal cells (informational). Not exercised by any captured round, on either side: the all-8-chunks-rejected retry (cursor + 1,000,000), and non-hex server seeds, where the site keys HMAC with UTF-8 bytes and this package with Buffer.from(hex). The live site file is compared with the same pins by scripts/check-site-verifier.mjs.

profileChecks.note: revealMines(serverSeed, clientSeed, nonce, mineCount) is recomputed for EVERY bet in the population — wins and losses alike, no filter — and compared with mineTiles by sameMines, which is ORDER-SENSITIVE (element by element, same length), so the comparison is the DRAW-ORDER list the operator serves rather than a sorted set; there is no tolerance. A skipped round is a failure, not a smaller sample: `skipped === 0` is part of the pass condition, and the denominator is EXPECTED_BETS from src/pins.ts rather than bets.length, so "6,900/6,900" cannot be true of whatever the file happens to contain

the draw-bias bound is stated IN THE STEP DETAIL as a computed quantity: maxFair for each of the 25 ranges the shuffle uses (read from src/rng.ts maxFairFor, the one ceiling the draw itself reads), the exact per-value bias conditional on acceptance (integer arithmetic, src/bias.ts drawBias on src/rng.ts maxFairFor), the worst per-draw rejection probability (4.889e-9 at range 25) and the rejection census over the population (0 of 172,500 draws, 2.024e-4 expected). The declared design is rejection sampling, so the gate is EXACT ZERO bias at every range (a fortiori ≤ 2^-32) — deliberately stricter than the bound, because a plain chunk % range with no rejection is biased by less than 2^-32 at every range 1..25 and would pass the bound alone. The branch the capture never takes is exercised on a vector inside the step (nonce 760455 / cursor 12 / range 13 must draw 6; deletion draws 1). Mutation M12 (maxFair = 2^32), a declared survivor until 2026-09-23, now FAILs this step. Scope, printed by the step: this bounds the AUDITOR'S draw; the operator's branch stays ASSUMED (MANIFEST DL-3)

the player-verifier parity arm. The Mines verifier a player uses on the ProvablyFair.org site — VerifyBets games/mines/derive.js and the one library file it imports, lib/hmac-sha256.js — is vendored byte-for-byte in verifier-parity/ and both files' SHA-256 digests are recorded in src/pins.ts SITE_VERIFIER_PINS (derive.js fa4dbd19…, hmac-sha256.js 2095571f…). The step hashes the vendored copies against the pins, loads them with only the ES-module keywords removed (src/site-verifier.ts; any other import or export form is a load FAIL), runs deriveMines on all 6,900 captured rounds and requires the draw-order minePositions to EQUAL src/rng.ts revealMines — the computeLayout every other layout step uses — with the denominator pinned to EXPECTED_BETS. Measured 2026-09-24: 6,900/6,900 equal (and 6,900/6,900 equal to the served mineTiles); displayCents equal at 300/300 legal cells (printed, not scored). Mutation M44 edits one byte of the vendored derive.js logic and this step FAILs on the hash; a re-pinned copy of the same edit FAILs on layout parity (probe 2026-09-24). scripts/check-site-verifier.mjs compares a site checkout with the same pins (exit 1 on mismatch). What this parity is: hash-pinned behavioural equality on every captured round, not a derive.js generated from src/rng.ts. Where the two differ, on inputs no captured round reaches: all eight chunks of a digest rejected (the site redraws at cursor + 1,000,000; src/rng.ts, rebuilt from docs/ALGORITHM.md, which leaves it unspecified (O1), throws), and non-hex server seeds (the site keys the HMAC with their UTF-8 bytes; src/rng.ts throws). The operator's own verify endpoint is a different thing and remains unprobed

steps.name: House Edge / RTP Audit (closed-form identity, per-config, anti-circular)
steps.detail: Closed-form identity theoreticalRTP(m,k) = winProbability(m,k) × minesMultiplierExact(m,k) (winProbability = pure C(25-m,k)/C(25,k) combinatorics), checked for m=1..24 at k=1 and Phase-E depths (m=3, k=1..5) — 28/28 cases: RTP range 99.0000%–99.0000%, mean 99.0000% — a clean 99.0000% for every (m,k) (closed-form edge exactly 1.00%), because the exact multiplier makes the CLOSED FORM identically (1 − edge) — the settlement floor can reduce the return, quantified next. Full-grid reference sweep: all 300/300 legal (m,k) cells (k=1..25−m) evaluate to 99.0000% within 1e-9 (0 off), range 99.0000%–99.0000% — this checks the reference formula at every reachable depth, NOT the operator (25/300 cells are live-witnessed via Step 8; 275 formula-only; additional settlement coverage is planned for production). Settlement floor: the identity above is the THEORETICAL leg; the amount actually credited is floor8(stake × multExact), so settled RTP is at most (1 − edge), with equality when no fractional settlement unit is discarded. Worst case over all 300 cells at the capture's smallest stake ($0.10, DERIVED from the 2 distinct betAmount values in the pinned bets — $0.10, $10.00 — not read from meta.phases; the header's own smallest amount is $0.10 and the two agree): m=2,k=3 loses 6.600e-8 of turnover → settled RTP 98.9999934%, i.e. 99.0000% to four decimals. Edge-rational integrity: EDGE_NUM/EDGE_DEN = 99000000/100000000 exactly represents (1 − HOUSE_EDGE) = 0.99 — the BigInt factor the floor8 credit identity in Step 8 divides by. A factor that only approximates the audited edge makes that identity measure a different edge, silently. Reference-formula integrity: 0 cells returned a non-finite value — a NaN/Infinity here is NOT an "off 99%" deviation (which FLAGs); it means the auditor's own reference is corrupt and every comparison built on it is vacuous, so it hard-FAILS. This is the uncapped reference calculation; Step 8 independently checks the recorded winningAmount at captured winning configurations. The displayed multiplier field is still floored — cosmetic (Step 7). Monotonicity (FLAG policy, scored): the exact multiplier is strictly increasing in depth and in mine count over 552/552 adjacent legal cell pairs (exact rational comparison) — 0 violations. Caps (MINES-14 cap half, MANIFEST DL-7) — DISCLOSED, NOT SCORED since 2026-10-15: payout caps are excluded from the audit and multiplier caps stay in scope (profile owner, 2026-10-15); LIQD states that Mines has had no multiplier cap since the end of August 2026 (the 10,000× setting removed from the configuration) and that a per-round payout limit ends the round and pays the full multiplier for the tiles already revealed (operator statement, 2026-10-15, quoted in MANIFEST DL-7). Cap figures as computed (not scored): quoted within the July setting yes, audited settings single-valued at it yes, scored build carries it no. RTP claim — OPEN RULING 1 (profile owner: which statement on LIQD's page is LIQD held to?): the held claim is the page's flat 99.00% ("99% RTP at every setting"; scored by the RTP-CLAIM gate printed after the steps). Printed for the ruling, not scored. FLAG REASONS: none.

profileChecks.note: the closed form at EVERY legal cell: the full-grid sweep evaluates all 300 legal (m,k) cells (m=1..24, k=1..25-m; the count is asserted === 300) and requires theoreticalRTP(m,k) = winProbability(m,k) x minesMultiplierExact(m,k) to equal PUBLISHED_RTP within 1e-9, which is algebraically the profile's claim that mult(m,k) = C(25,k)/C(25-m,k) x (1-edge). The two factors are INDEPENDENTLY WRITTEN in src/config.ts — winProbability as the binomial ratio via combination(), minesMultiplierExact as the product (1-edge) x prod (25-i)/(25-m-i) — and Step 13 anchors the probability factor against a product form and an integer subset tally, so this is not the module agreeing with itself. PUBLISHED_RTP = 0.99 is deliberately a LITERAL and not 1 - HOUSE_EDGE, which would make the comparison vacuous. A corrupted cell is caught: M05 sets minesMultiplierExact(4,2) to 1 and this step FLAGs; M04 sets it to NaN and it FAILs

the identity half of anti-circularity — P(survive to k) x multiplier(m,k) == (1-edge) at all 300 legal cells with no operator data anywhere in the computation. Non-finite is separated from off-target as its own fault class, because Math.abs(NaN - 0.99) > 1e-9 is FALSE and an unguarded sweep would print "300/300 clean": a cell at 70% FLAGs, a cell that is not a number hard-FAILS.
